proof_dependencies.basis: Gamma root annuli, composition in the binomial basis, and endpoint normalization reduce the support. The short support tail also applies the Padé inequality.
At a prime, both reciprocal polynomials restrict the widths and multiplicities of a possible common factor. Short factorial blocks force prime divisibility and sharply reduce the finite computation.

Section 4 derives the rotated truncations and nonzero monomial Wronskian, including the simple-pole coefficients and p-adic progression estimates. The large-order arguments derive monotonic extensions of the independently checked endpoints. Nguyen-Dang's preprint provides the Laguerre template.

Appendix B proves constant-support squarefreeness. Appendix C proves the physical-shape derivative bridge and the prime-power branch, including the adjoint rank condition and Artin–Hasse descent. The accompanying written Positive-exponent Boundary contour proof gives the three unbounded branches. Exact arithmetic covers the finite domains and the numerical contour guards.

answers.contribution: Consecutive coprimality for all normalized moment-polynomial pairs of univariate binomials over fields of characteristic zero.
answers.conceptual_reason: Shared Newton slopes and factorial prime support restrict possible factors. A nonzero Padé resultant in the remaining unbounded region has incompatible divisibility and complex size bounds.
answers.hardest_step: Lemma 14 and its explicit tail identity are on pp. 10–13. Appendix D reduces the intermediate region, and Appendix E, pp. 34–40, closes the large-order Padé comparison.
answers.limitations: Two terms in one variable in characteristic zero. The proof includes exact finite computations and certified parameter comparisons.
answers.verification_obstacles: The three contour proofs, numerical enclosures and finite verifiers are supplied separately. The PDF identifies where they enter. The reader traced the partial fractions, terminal ranges and contour dependencies in the revised PDF.

answers.contribution: Uniform consecutive coprimality for all univariate binomial supports and all positive consecutive orders in characteristic zero.
answers.conceptual_reason: A pair of Newton polygons restricts a common factor at every prime. In the large range the Padé gap forces divisibility of a nonzero resultant, and rotational averaging yields an incompatible complex upper bound.
answers.hardest_step: Lemma 14 in Section 4 gives the norm comparison. Proposition 23 in Appendix E closes its hardest application by separating Newton heights and counting square multiples close to the factorial endpoints.
answers.limitations: The theorem is for two terms in one variable in characteristic zero. It concerns consecutive coprimality. The proof uses finite exact checks and certified numerical comparisons along with the uniform estimates.
answers.verification_obstacles: The written Positive-exponent Boundary appendix is needed for Lemma 20, and the exact programs are needed to reproduce the computational parts. The final PDF explicitly identifies those two parts of the separately supplied supplement. The blind reader independently reproduced finite set sizes in Proposition 7 and Appendices B and C.
